inlines.v: This chapter is a PiCar-X Companion addition — it is not part of SunFounder's official documentation. Every Hermes command below comes from the official
, and the PiCar-X skill and test tool are the same ones SunFounder ships for OpenClaw (see
Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent from
. Like OpenClaw, it goes beyond chat: it understands natural language instructions and can actually run commands, manage files, and call tools on your Raspberry Pi. Two things set it apart:
Hermes automatically creates new skills from your conversations and refines them over time, building an agent that gets better at the tasks you actually give it.
It builds memory that persists across sessions — tell it once how you like your PiCar-X driven, and it remembers.
You can talk to it through the CLI on the Pi itself, or connect it to Telegram, Discord, email, and other messaging platforms via its gateway.
Hermes Agent requires a model with at least a
— smaller models are rejected at startup. Community Raspberry Pi guides recommend a
Pi 4 or Pi 5 with 4 GB+ RAM
, pointed at a hosted LLM provider (the model runs in the cloud; the Pi only runs the agent loop). Like OpenClaw, the Pi Zero 2W (512 MB) is not enough.
Open the terminal on your Raspberry Pi and run the official install script. It handles all dependencies (Python 3.11, Node.js 22, ripgrep, ffmpeg) automatically:

items.html: curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash

inlines.v: On a headless Pi you don't need browser automation — the installer supports a
flag that skips the Playwright/Chromium download. See the official installation guide for details. Because new versions are updated rapidly, it's normal if your installation steps differ slightly.

items.html: source ~/.bashrc
hermes setup

sections.title: Making Hermes Agent Operate the PiCar-X

inlines.v: The same PiCar-X Skill, a different agent.
The PiCar-X skill that SunFounder ships for OpenClaw is a portable skill bundle: a
file (safety rules, code templates, and the mapping from natural language to Python code) plus a
command-line tool. Hermes Agent reads the same
format, so the identical bundle teaches Hermes to drive your car:
Drive forward, backward, turn left/right with steering servo control
Pan left/right, tilt up/down via the 2-axis camera gimbal
Read ultrasonic distance and grayscale data for line tracking and cliff detection
Play sound effects and music through the car's speaker
Take photos, detect faces, track colors, recognize QR codes, gestures, and traffic signs
Before you can use the PiCar-X skill with Hermes, make sure you have:
properly assembled and connected to your Raspberry Pi
You can verify the libraries by running:

blocks.html: python3 -c "import picarx"

inlines.v: If this command runs without errors, you're ready to proceed.

Q. PiCar-X doesn't respond to commands.
First verify that PiCar-X is properly connected and powered on, then test basic functionality directly:

blocks.html: python3 ~/.hermes/skills/picarx-control/scripts/pc.py sensor distance

inlines.v: If this fails, ensure the required Python libraries are installed:

blocks.code: python3 -c "import picarx; import robot_hat; import vilib"

inlines.v: Q. PiCar-X movements seem jerky or the steering is off-center.
This usually means servo calibration values are off. Run the calibration tool, or use a lower speed (for example

blocks.html: python3 ~/.hermes/skills/picarx-control/scripts/pc.py calibrate

inlines.v: OpenClaw and Hermes Agent can coexist on the same Raspberry Pi — they install to different locations and each reads its own copy of the skill bundle. If you try both, just remember only one of them should drive the car at a time.
